title: The Celestin Tuxedo band members and the barbershop
summary: He names Clarence Hall, Foots Sims, Adam Cato and Andy Anderson, and describes John Josephs' barbershop as a gathering place for musicians.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who were in the Celestin -- it was called the Tuxedo orchestra, Tuxedo Jazz Band? Who were some of your fellow band members in that orchestra? That was about 1939 we're talking about?
They had Clarence Hall who was the brother of Edmund Hall, and who else did they have, they

S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC.
WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

had Foots Sims playing drums and Adam Cato played piano and who else -- Anderson, Andy Anderson played trumpet, but it was Clarence Hall who reminded me of the real New Orleans style of blowing. And he would bounce along with that rhythm. He gets his rhythm by moving up and down his chair. He would just blow out a storm. He never left New Orleans. He was a typical New Orleans style musician. They were great the way they were. I was so pleased that I was able to be in New Orleans. Now, in New Orleans, there's a barber shop there that is run by a fellow by the name of John Josephs. He's a base player and in this barber shop there was a focal point where musicians around New Orleans would come for their gigs and casual engagements and chew the fat and talk about other musicians and subjects in general, Depression, or whatever you want to talk about. They all get together and they have a ball right there in that barber shop.
Did they ever bring their instruments over and jam sometimes?
No, I can't recall, but I have seen some instruments all piled up in one corner of the barber shop, some band had left there to go on a tour and they left it there to go to their homes

wherever they're going to stay and they left their instruments there.
What kind of jobs did Kid Rene' and "Papa" Celestin play exactly? I mean, they played dances -- did they play for colleges?
